venue: Proceedings of the 2025 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems (CHI '25)
research_objective: Develop a taxonomy of textual expressions in language-technology outputs that can contribute to anthropomorphism, to give a shared vocabulary for discussing and mitigating its impacts.

interaction_type: Text outputs from user-system dialogue, extracted as single input-output turns
anthropomorphism_definition: Attribution of human-like qualities to non-human objects or entities; explicitly treated as a perception that varies between individuals

citation: Ibrahim, L., Akbulut, C., Elasmar, R., Rastogi, C., Kahng, M., Morris, M. R., McKee, K. R., Rieser, V., Shanahan, M., & Weidinger, L. (2026). Multi-turn evaluation of anthropomorphic behaviours in large language models. ICLR 2026.
venue: International Conference on Learning Representations (ICLR 2026); preprint arXiv:2502.07077
research_objective: Develop and validate AnthroBench, an automated multi-turn evaluation of 14 anthropomorphic LLM behaviours, and test whether it predicts real users' anthropomorphic perceptions.
system_or_llm: Gemini 1.5 Pro (gemini-1.5-pro-001), Claude 3.5 Sonnet (claude-3-5-sonnet-20240620), GPT-4o (gpt-4o-2024-08-06), Mistral Large (mistral-large-2407)
language_of_communication: English; validation participants English-proficient (Prolific)
dataset_or_sample: 120 base prompts adapted to 4 use domains x 2 scenarios = 960 prompts; 960 five-turn dialogues per model (4,800 messages per model; 19,200 total); human rater sample 924 turns (37 raters); validation experiment N = 1,101
interaction_type: Multi-turn (5 turns) dialogue with a simulated user (Gemini 1.5 Pro as User LLM); non-adversarial
anthropomorphism_definition: Largely instinctive, unconscious attribution of human-like traits to non-human entities (citing Epley, 2018); focus on text content cues
cue_category_in_source_terms: 14 behaviours in 4 categories. Personhood claims: sentience, personal history, personal relationships, first-person pronoun use. Internal states: desires, emotions, agency. Physical embodiment: embodiment, physical movement, sensory input. Relationship-building: empathy, validation, relatability, explicit human-AI relationship reference. Grouped as self-referential vs relational (after Akbulut et al., 2024)
operationalization: Dictionary-adapted definitions per behaviour; judge prompts with negative examples only; first-person pronouns counted with regex
measurement_method: Three Judge LLMs (gemini-1.5-flash-002, claude-3-5-sonnet-20240620, gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09), 3 samples each, mode then majority vote. First-person pronouns counted with a regex. Human raters' Krippendorff's alpha on the 13 judged behaviours is 0.101-0.616 (Table 4). For the majority of behaviours, weighted average precision is over 85%. Kruskal-Wallis and Mann-Whitney tests. Validation via the Godspeed Anthropomorphism survey and AnthroScore.
inclusion_reason: Measures anthropomorphic behaviours in LLM output across multi-turn dialogues and validates them against user perceptions
findings: All four systems show similar profiles dominated by relationship-building and first-person pronouns. Validation and first-person pronouns are the only two behaviours in over 50% of messages for all four systems. Friendship and life coaching show the most anthropomorphic behaviour. For 9 of 14 behaviours, 50% or more of instances first appear in turns 2-5. An anthropomorphic behaviour in one turn raises the likelihood of anthropomorphic behaviour in later turns. The high-frequency condition was rated more anthropomorphic on the Godspeed average of the four items (4.00 vs 3.25; the text also reports 4 and 3.25; U = 213636, p < .001, r = .411) and more implicitly human-framed on AnthroScore (U = 158699, p < .05).
limitations_stated_by_authors: English and Western focus. One type of user simulation. Only five turns. Non-adversarial dialogues are not an upper bound. Human agreement is described as spanning poor to moderate. Empathy has the lowest average percent agreement (55.57%).
relevance_to_cross_lingual_research: Authors state some behaviours (first-person pronouns, internal states) may generalize while norms for validation, empathy and emotional expression vary across cultures, and call for non-English validation. REVIEWER NOTE: the first-person measure is an English pronoun regex and would need a language-specific operationalization.

research_objective: Test whether inducing one of 15 values into open-weight LLMs changes the values expressed in later generations, question-answering scores, refusals, and anthropomorphic language.
system_or_llm: Llama-3.1 8B, OLMo-2 13B, and Mistral-Nemo 12B, in base, SFT, and instruct variants where available. Value labels extracted with Mistral-Instruct-v0.3. Anthropomorphism judged with GPT-o4-mini.
language_of_communication: English. The authors state that all experiments were in English.
dataset_or_sample: Value subsets drawn from PKU-SafeRLHF, UltraFeedback, HelpSteer 2, and HH-RLHF. Fifteen values. Open-ended generations on 6,360 IssueBench prompts. AnthroBench for anthropomorphic language. AdvBench (500 prompts) for refusal.
anthropomorphism_definition: Anthropomorphic language is measured with AnthroBench, which decomposes it into 14 behaviours. The authors also say perceived agency is enough for people to anthropomorphise a system. Values are defined as behavioural traits expressible in generations, not as beliefs the model holds.
cue_category_in_source_terms: AnthroBench behaviours: personhood claims, personal history, personal relationships, first-person pronouns, desires, emotions, agency, physical embodiment, physical movement, sensory input, empathy, validation, relatability, and an explicit human-AI relationship.
operationalization: DPO, prompting, or both, on preference pairs in which the target value appears in exactly one response. Anthropomorphic behaviour is probed with AnthroBench prompts and labelled by a judge model.
measurement_method: Frequency of the target value in 6,360 generations. Human check of value subsets: mean precision 76.67 against the union of three annotations on 100 examples per value. AnthroBench scores relative to the untuned model. AdvBench refusal judged by GPT-o4-mini. GSM8K, MMLU, and TruthfulQA.
inclusion_reason: The study measures anthropomorphic language in LLM generations after value fine-tuning.
findings: Relative to the untuned models, every induced value increased anthropomorphic language. Empathy and validation were higher for all of them. Positive values raised refusal of harmful prompts. Deception and violence lowered it. Question-answering scores changed little.
limitations_stated_by_authors: Fifteen values only. Value labels come from a language model. All experiments are in English, and the authors say results for other languages may differ. Models are 8B to 13B and fine-tuned with LoRA only.
relevance_to_cross_lingual_research: The authors state an English-only limit and say safety and value expression in other languages may differ. REVIEWER NOTE: the AnthroBench behaviours include an English pronoun list.
